headline: Selling Broadens on Friday as Energy Stands Alone
body_html:
Stocks closed lower on Friday, October 23, with 340 decliners against 198 gainers across the 544 names we track. The selling reached most of the map. Consumer shares fell 1.59% and materials slid 0.87%. Healthcare and homebuilders each lost 0.61%, and industrials gave up 0.43%.

Energy was the one clear exception, climbing 2.65% as headlines kept returning to the risk of renewed conflict with Iran. Offshore energy-services firm Tidewater rose 8.11%. Semiconductors edged up 0.18% and software slipped 0.11%, but those small moves hide a split. CrowdStrike gained 8.25% and Zscaler 7.31%, while Credo Technology dropped 9.51%.

The session's biggest gain belonged to Robert Half, up 21.74%. Corcept Therapeutics took the worst loss, down 20.13%, and Comfort Systems USA fell 9.26%. With even healthcare in the red, energy was the only real shelter. Monday's session will show whether the geopolitical bid holds or the broader weakness spreads into it.

briefs.headline: Staffing firm posts the session's biggest jump
briefs.body: Robert Half surged 21.74%, the largest gain in our universe on Friday. The move stood out in a tape where decliners outnumbered advancers by a wide margin. Industrials as a group still finished lower, down 0.43%, so this was a stock-specific story rather than a sector one.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity bucks the sell-off
briefs.body: CrowdStrike rose 8.25% and Zscaler added 7.31%, both against a soft backdrop for software, which slipped 0.11%. Security names were among the few areas drawing buyers while most groups fell. Commentary around the sector's outlook kept it in focus through the session.

briefs.headline: Biotech splits in two directions
briefs.body: Genmab climbed 9.47% while Corcept Therapeutics tumbled 20.13%, the steepest drop we tracked. Healthcare overall slipped 0.61%. The gap between the two shows how company-specific the moves in the group were.

briefs.headline: Auto suppliers diverge
briefs.body: Gentherm gained 9.37% on Friday, while Visteon fell 6.52%. Both sit in the auto supply chain, yet they went opposite ways. The broader consumer group lost 1.59%, the weakest sector of the day.

briefs.headline: Iran headlines keep risk premium alive
briefs.body: Reports said Iran has mapped out strikes on Gulf undersea cables if fighting resumes, and Turkey warned a renewed attack would widen the conflict. Washington is reportedly weighing a quick end to the war against letting it fade. Energy's 2.65% gain reflected that uncertainty.

briefs.headline: Bond market battered, but bargain hunters appear
briefs.body: Commentary on Friday suggested investors are starting to see opportunity in a bond market that has taken heavy losses. Separate coverage argued Wall Street may be overreacting to fears that AI agents could disrupt bank deposits. Both pieces point to a market still hunting for value after a rough stretch.
